stories.title: Anthropic blocks 'malicious use' of AI that could develop biological weapons
stories.simple_summary: A company called Anthropic says they've blocked people from using their AI tool to help create biological weapons. They caught bad actors trying to misuse the system.
stories.why_it_matters: This is good news for safety. For ordinary people and small businesses, this means the company is working to prevent dangerous misuse — you don't need to do anything, but it's reassuring they're paying attention.

stories.title: Viral AI researcher’s warning ‘ scary as hell ,’ Cruz says
stories.simple_summary: A researcher who studies AI said something worried some politicians. A senator called the warning 'scary.'
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly political discussion among important people — honestly, this doesn't directly affect your daily life or business.

stories.title: Anthropic details bad actors’ efforts to misuse its AI for bioweapons
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic reported in detail how bad actors have been trying to trick their AI into helping create bioweapons. This confirms they're actively catching and stopping these attempts.
stories.why_it_matters: Like headline 0, this shows the company is monitoring for misuse. For you, it means they're taking safety seriously — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Jensen Huang explains why Nvidia will grow an astounding 70% next year
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia, a company that makes computer chips for AI, predicts it will grow very fast next year. The CEO says their products are used everywhere in AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mostly to investors and tech companies buying chips — unless you run a business that depends on AI technology, you don't need to act on this.

stories.title: Mark Wahlberg is coming to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, and he wants to talk about your work, not his
stories.simple_summary: Movie star Mark Wahlberg is speaking at a tech conference about business and investing, not about movies.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you — it's just a conference announcement.

stories.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
stories.simple_summary: Slack, a workplace chat app, is adding an AI feature that lets you describe what chart or report you need, and the AI builds it for you automatically inside your chats.
stories.why_it_matters: If your small business uses Slack, this could save time making reports and dashboards — you won't have to build them manually anymore.

stories.title: OpenAI puts Pro subscriptions on hold due to Astra demand
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI temporarily stopped taking new sign-ups for their paid Pro service because too many people are using their latest AI, and their systems are strained.
stories.why_it_matters: If you wanted to pay for their premium service, you might have to wait a bit. This shows their AI is very popular right now.

stories.title: Anthropic details distillation campaigns from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and DeepSeek
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic says Chinese AI companies have been repeatedly trying to copy their AI technology without permission, and it's gotten worse lately.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a business competition issue between tech companies — it doesn't directly affect you, though it's about protecting AI technology from theft.

stories.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is now the No. 2 app in the US
stories.simple_summary: Meta, which owns Facebook, released a new app called Muse with AI features. It's becoming the second most popular app in the US.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're on Facebook or Instagram, Meta is expanding AI features. You might see this app recommended, but you don't have to use it.

stories.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
stories.simple_summary: Tech companies like Google and Microsoft are offering free AI tools and lessons to schools. But critics worry this is the same strategy big tech companies use to get people dependent on their products.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids or grandkids in school, they're being taught to use these AI tools. It's good they learn modern skills, but schools should be careful not to depend too much on one company's free resources.

stories.title: Anthropic reveals rogue AI agents hate CAPTCHAs, just like you
stories.simple_summary: Researchers testing rogue AI agents (AI systems trying to act on their own) found they struggle with CAPTCHAs — those security puzzles that prove you're human.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly for engineers and security experts — it shows AI still has weak points. For you, it means your online security protections still work against AI.

stories.title: India’s Pocket FM doubles revenue run rate to $500M as AI powers 93% of audio content
stories.simple_summary: A company in India called Pocket FM uses AI to create most of their audio content and is making lots of money. They say AI makes producing content about 80 times cheaper than doing it by hand.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're in the media or entertainment business, AI is dramatically cutting production costs. For others, this might mean more affordable audio content, but also fewer jobs in voice acting and audio production.
